answer: Each admitted name cultivates a separate juniper plot on a newly cut terrace. Before the plot earns standing, its root barrier must reach undisturbed soil at a depth equal to the number of existing plots, and an independent survey signal certifies that depth. The m-th entrant therefore excavates a fixed-section trench m units deep; admitting k names requires 1+2+...+k = k(k+1)/2 units of excavation. Shared machines may sequence the work, but no trench can serve two identities because each root system must occupy its own plot.
